Update (Alpha/3).

Improved the overall design of the template file, added some simple menu
link options making use of Javascript, added multilingual support (some
certain i18n strings for some certain languages not yet translated, but
most of it is finished; 11 different language options provided at the
moment), added a LICENSE file (I've opted to use the MIT License, to
maximise permissiveness), and, most importantly, the script now
correctly utilises batch/bulk queries, querying multiple IPs
simultaneously from SFS, rather than querying each IP individually.
Still haven't yet implemented any hard-coded limitations (such as the
planned limitation based upon API daily quota rate limits), haven't yet
created README or Changelog files and haven't yet implemented any
significant safe-guards. Querying using the old XML format has been
completely abandoned in favour of using serialised results, which is
cleaner, more efficient, easier to process and was easier to work with
for coding in the ability to perform batch/bulk queries. The script is
now entirely stable and safe to use, but, I'm leaving it marked as
"Alpha" for now, rather than kicking it to "Beta", because I haven't yet
implemented to ability to return results in multiple formats, as was
possible with the old version of the script that ran via my old CMS, and
I'd still like to do this at some point. This is the final "Alpha"
commit; The next commit with be the initial "Beta" commit.

Update (Alpha/2).

Code is now stable, and more usable.. But there's still a lot of work to
be done. Adding multiple output options, appropriate safeguards, quota
rate limiting and monitoring, multilingual support and appropriate
documentation (of any kind, including LICENSE, README and Changelog
files), hasn't yet been done, but, the script does, in fact, work
correctly now. The script can distinguish between listed and not listed
results, can determine if a result (or a submitted IP address) is
erroneous, can automatically fetch the latest "bannedips.csv" file from
SFS, caches all results and will clear the cache after 1 day (for clean
and erroneous results) or 1 week (for non-clean, listed results).
Multiple IPs can be queried, but no hard-coded limitation to this has
been coded yet, and they're queried to SFS individual, rather than
collectively (the script will need to be able to batch query at some
point in the near future).

Update (ALPHA).

First commit containing working code. It's barely usable, and it kind of
works.. But it's definitely not yet finished; A crapload more work still
needs to be done. You can use it at this point if you want, but I'd
strongly advise against doing so in a production environment (better to
wait until a future commit containing more stable code is available),
and you should make sure that only you have access to your copy. I'll
write up some installation and usage instructions in the future, but I
haven't had time to do so yet (anyone with any PHP experience should be
able to work it out reasonably easily, though).

Update (Pre-ALPHA).

Still no working code committed yet, and the project is still pre-ALPHA
at this point. This commit could've waited, but, mostly, I wanted to
commit something to show that I'm not entirely ignoring this project,
and that work is still being done. This commit includes the SFS favicon
("favicon.ico") and "template.html", which'll be used as an HTML
template for anything and everything displayed by the SFS MASS IP
Checker. I'd expected to have working code available within a few days
of my originally creating this repo, but, my week has been busier than
expected and other commitments have taken priority. Working code should
be available within the coming week, though.
